title: Quaintly Simmered Algerian Lamb Tagine
description: A savory and light Algerian dish featuring lamb and meringue nests, simmered in a nimono-style broth, this recipe is perfect for a special occasion. It is also low-sodium-friendly, making it a great option for those with dietary restrictions.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until it is softened and lightly browned, about 8 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the lamb pieces and cook until they are browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add the cumin, coriander, and cayenne pepper and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the low-sodium chicken broth and bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, until the lamb is tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
About 30 minutes before serving, place the meringue nests on top of the tagine and cover the pot.
Serve the tagine hot, garnished with fresh parsley and lemon wedges if desired.
Cook poultry to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F before serving.
